title: Quantum-inspired classical simulation through randomized time evolution
summary: Tensor-network simulations of quantum many-body dynamics are fundamentally limited by entanglement build-up, which leads to exponentially growing computational costs. Furthermore, these classical simulation algorithms are inherently sequential as typically a tensor network representation of the quantum state is updated incrementally at each time step. We build on recently introduced randomized quantum algorithms for time evolution (TE-PAI), and adapt them to the classical simulation context with the purpose of enabling massive parallelisation.
